kypExtensions.summary: The staircase grammar of the cultural formulation interview: the five printed Identify moves read as one descent — PROBLEM (the problem through the patient's perspective, in their own words or the words they would use with family and friends) → PERCEPTION (why they think they are experiencing the problem — the perceived cause) → BACKGROUND (what makes it better or worse; family, community, spirituality) → PLAN (concerns or suggestions about the current plan; the COMBINE rule — if they do not want to follow medical advice, investigate combining their plans with the standard medical regimen, never overriding) → BARRIERS (anything preventing care in a standard medical institution; the closing probe for what may increase the chance of maintaining a good patient-physician relationship). The claim 'each move feeds the next; the relationship is the deliverable' is the KYP synthesis of the printed sequence.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the five moves as parallel sentences; the ordered-staircase reading, the one-word decoders (PROBLEM/PERCEPTION/BACKGROUND/PLAN/BARRIERS), and the relationship-as-output framing are KYP's organization.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea DECODER 1 + mechanisms[0] cultural-formulation-flow + blocks[2] the steps block + the registry visual's Zone A staircase and KYP-reading card

kypExtensions.summary: The safety architecture of trauma-informed care: the printed rules re-organized by function — SCREEN (thorough behavioral health screenings; regularly assess mood, substance use, social supports, and suicide risk), FOCUS (trauma-related symptoms that interfere with social and occupational function, not the narrative), PROTECT (PERMISSION — ask permission prior to discussion, never invasive questions requiring the patient to describe trauma in detail; SIGNAL — before the physical exam, the patient may signal to end it immediately; SUPPORT — additional staff, counseling offered or advised) — with the 4 R's (Realize, Recognize, Respond, Resist retraumatization) as First Aid's own compression, and the KYP rule 'PERMISSION governs the conversation, SIGNAL governs the exam, SUPPORT governs the room'.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the rules as a paragraph; the screen/focus/protect grouping, the PERMISSION·SIGNAL·SUPPORT triad, and the control-transfer reading are KYP's organization. The 4 R's mnemonic itself is FA's own (red-initialed in print, attributed, not counted as a KYP mnemonic).
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea DECODER 2 + blocks[3] the trauma rules list + the registry visual's Zone B panel and 4 R's strip + mnemonics[3] PERMISSION, SIGNAL, SUPPORT

kypExtensions.summary: The motivational-interviewing arc: RESOLVE AMBIVALENCE (a counseling technique to facilitate behavior modification; useful for many conditions, eg, nicotine dependence, obesity; some desire to change required, commitment explicitly NOT) → EXAMINE the behavior (how it interferes with their life or why they might want to change it — the patient voices the argument) → ASSESS BARRIERS (eg, food access — structural; untreated trauma — psychological) → READINESS guides physician-suggested goals → SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time bound — FA's own, red-initialed); plus the KYP rule 'readiness SIZES the goal; SMART FORMATS it' and the MI-vs-directive-advice contrast (who supplies the argument for change).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the sentences; the arc organization, the candidacy formula's two-sided reading (some desire = required; commitment = not), the structural/psychological barrier pairing, and the MI-vs-directive contrast are KYP's design. SMART itself is FA's own (attributed).
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[1] ambivalence-to-smart-arc + blocks[4] the MI decoder list + blocks[6] the compare block + the registry visual's Zone C arc

kypExtensions.summary: The checklist organization of gender- and sexuality-inclusive history taking: NO ASSUMPTIONS (sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, and behavior are independent axes — a patient who identifies as heterosexual may engage in same-sex sexual activity) · NEUTRAL TERMS ('partner' rather than 'husband' or 'wife' upon first meeting, until the patient instructs otherwise or uses specific pronouns) · SEX AT BIRTH ≠ GENDER IDENTITY · ONLY IF RELEVANT (the hand-laceration rule — do not bring up gender or sexuality if not relevant to the visit) · PRONOUNS + EMR (state yours, eg, 'I'm Dr. Smith, and I use she/her pronouns'; ask how patients would like to be addressed; correct name and pronouns in the electronic medical record) · CONFIDENTIALITY + TRUST (reassure confidentiality; patients may not be open to others in their life; trust is built over time).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the rules as flowing paragraphs; the six-item checklist shape, the four-independent-axes reading, and the relevance-gate framing shared with the disabilities rules on the previous page are KYP's organization.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea DECODER 4 + blocks[5] the checklist table + the registry visual's Zone D strip + clinical block items

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed page — 4 patterns (the five-move cultural formulation stem, the trauma-rules stem with permission/signal/support, the MI + SMART goal-format stem, the inclusive-wording stem), 4 traps (detail-account vs permission-first; commitment required vs some desire; combine vs persuade/override; universal identity questionnaire vs the relevance gate), 3 pivots (the respectful-option router, readiness-sizes vs SMART-formats, the signal promised BEFORE the exam), and 8 recall cards covering all four blocks.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the techniques only; the attack structure, distractor designs, and question shapes are KYP's design.
